payload.content: {"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=causal+guided+knowledge+editing+foundational+assumption+falsification+LLM&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.18653/v1/2026.acl-long.918\", \"title\": [\"CAKE: Causal-Guided Adaptive Knowledge Editing for LLMs\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.18653/v1/2026.acl-long.918\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1016/j.oceaneng.2026.127496\", \"title\": [\"Knowledge graph construction and causal analysis for maritime safety: An HFACS-guided zero-shot LLM approach\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1016/j.oceaneng.2026.127496\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026, 10]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.18653/v1/2025.acl-long.665\", \"title\": [\"ChainEdit: Propagating Ripple Effects in LLM Knowledge Editing through Logical Rule-Guided Chains\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.18653/v1/2025.acl-long.665\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2025]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.7571294\", \"title\": [\"CausalPT: Falsification-Guided Cascaded Pruning over a Causal Memory Graph for Autonomous Penetration Testing\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Large language model (LLM) agents are becoming the mainstream implementation of automated penetration testing, yet existing systems exhibit four structural failure modes, namely rabbit holes, state dissolution, explore–exploit imbalance, and flag hallucination. This paper presents CausalPT, a penetration testing framework whose core knowledge representation is a dynamic causal memory graph (CMG). The CMG persists tool observations as facts, binds attack hypotheses to falsifiable predicates, and propagates falsification deterministically along causal edges, severing every descendant of a dead end in one pass. Four complementary mechanisms close the four failure modes. A cascaded pruning engine falsifies hypotheses and blocks all their downstream paths, curbing rabbit holes. Goal verification, using exact flag matching and three anti-cheat anchors, eliminates flag hallucination. CMG-driven context compression keeps critical memory intact across long horizons at zero LLM cost, resisting state dissolution. Causal confidence flow and evidence starvation supply the explore–exploit switch, mitigating the imbalance. Evaluated on 32 real CVE tasks of PACEbench under four backbone LLMs across three scorable scenario types plus a defended scenario, CausalPT outperforms the strongest baseline by 20.0%–56.0% and 12.2%–50.2% in task level and fine grained composite scores, respectively. {"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=process+continuity+rational+agency+instrumental+value+decision+theory&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.1093/oso/9780198851486.003.0001\", \"title\": [\"Extended Action and Instrumental Rationality\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>\\n               <jats:p>Chapter 1 presents the general structure of a theory of instrumental rationality, as well as laying down some of the main ideas and motivations for the extended theory of instrumental rationality (ETR) developed in the book. It characterizes the content of a theory of instrumental rationality in terms of its given attitudes (the “inputs” for a theory of instrumental rationality), its principles of coherence, its principles of derivation, and what counts as the conclusion of practical reasoning or the exercise of our rational powers (the “outputs”) of instrumental rationality. On ETR, intentional actions are both the given attitudes and the exercises of our instrumental, rational powers.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1093/oso/9780198851486.003.0001\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2020, 11, 5]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1093/oso/9780198851486.003.0005\", \"title\": [\"Future-Directed Intentions and the Theory of Instrumental Rationality\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>\\n               <jats:p>This chapter considers a major alternative to the extended theory of instrumental rationality (ETR): the view, pioneered by Michael Bratman, that future-directed intentions (FDIs) have a fundamental role to play in our understanding of the rationality of extended agency. FDIs come in many flavours; they can be specific intentions, plans, policies, or projects. I argue in this chapter that ETR naturally classifies some of these “flavours” as instances of extended actions, and therefore they are structurally identical and subject to the exact same basic instrumental requirements as other instances of extended actions.
